chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from 'Abd Sahih (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of a male slave, when he maraws a free woman or marries the female slave of another people, belongs to the slave; and if he marries his master's female slave, the one who separates them is he (the master), if he wishes, and he can take her from him without divorce.
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to divorce a male slave who marries his master's slave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the nuanced marital rights of a male slave (*abd*), distinguishing between his autonomy when marrying a free woman or another slave versus his master's prerogative when he marries the master's own slave (*walidah*). It highlights the economic and social hierarchy in early Islamic jurisprudence, where the master retains the right to dissolve the union without formal divorce (*talaq*) if the wife is his property, reflecting the interplay between personal status and ownership rights in Shia fiqh.
